    11 — Real global data on the globe¶

    The other globe notebooks build the base map; this one drapes real, whole-world datasets over the globe with the projected-map API. The data is WorldClim v2.1 (10-arc-minute, global EPSG:4326 GeoTIFFs, worldclim.org):

    • elevation (wc2.1_10m_elev) — a 2160x1080 global DEM, and
    • monthly average temperature (wc2.1_10m_tavg) — 12 global grids.

    The data is reprojected to each display CRS by pyramids, drawn on a plain axes by cleopatra, and framed into a globe by Digital-Earth — field / contours / pcolormesh all work on a projection. Ocean cells are nodata in WorldClim, so the ocean() disc shows through the sea automatically.

    The download cell caches into examples/data/global/ (git-ignored) and is skipped once the files are present. It needs network on first run; everything after is offline.

    This notebook also adds ETOPO global relief & bathymetry (NOAA, served downsampled by the CoastWatch ERDDAP). Unlike the land-only WorldClim grids, ETOPO covers the ocean floor too — a single field from the deep trenches (about -10 km) to the high peaks (about +8 km), so the whole globe is data.

    Read the committed data (cached)¶

    Fetch and unzip the two WorldClim products into the local cache.

    In [1]:
    Copied! 
    from pathlib import Path

# The half-degree global rasters are committed under examples/data/global/, so this notebook
# runs offline. They are WorldClim 2.1 10-arc-minute tavg/elev and NOAA ETOPO180, resampled to
# 0.5 deg (360 x 720) - the same grid the bundled ersstv5.nc uses, and finer than a page-sized
# globe resolves. See examples/data/ATTRIBUTION.md for the sources and licences.
CACHE = Path('../../examples/data/global')

ELEV = CACHE / 'worldclim_elev.tif'
TAVG = sorted(CACHE.glob('worldclim_tavg_*.tif'))      # 12 monthly grids, Jan..Dec
print('elevation:', ELEV.name)
print('temperature months:', len(TAVG))
    from pathlib import Path # The half-degree global rasters are committed under examples/data/global/, so this notebook # runs offline. They are WorldClim 2.1 10-arc-minute tavg/elev and NOAA ETOPO180, resampled to # 0.5 deg (360 x 720) - the same grid the bundled ersstv5.nc uses, and finer than a page-sized # globe resolves. See examples/data/ATTRIBUTION.md for the sources and licences.     Read with pyramids¶

    Load the global rasters as Datasets and define a graceful-coastlines helper.

    In [2]:
    Copied! 
    %matplotlib inline
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from pyramids.dataset import Dataset, GeoReference
from digitalearth.static import Map, projections

elevation = Dataset.read_file(str(ELEV))
jan = Dataset.read_file(str(TAVG[0]))
jul = Dataset.read_file(str(TAVG[6]))
print('elevation grid:', elevation.rows, 'x', elevation.columns, 'EPSG', elevation.epsg)
print('temperature grid:', jul.rows, 'x', jul.columns, 'EPSG', jul.epsg)

def context(m, *, coast=True):
    """Add coastlines if Natural Earth is reachable; never raise (keeps the notebook running offline)."""
    if not coast:
        return
    try:
        m.coastlines(resolution='110m')
    except Exception as exc:
        print('coastlines unavailable:', type(exc).__name__)
    %matplotlib inline import matplotlib.pyplot as plt from pyramids.dataset import Dataset, GeoReference from digitalearth.static import Map, projections elevation = Dataset.read_file(str(ELEV)) jan = Dataset.read_file(str(TAVG[0])) jul = Dataset.read_file(str(TAVG[6])) print('elevation grid:', elevation.rows, 'x', elevation.columns, 'EPSG', elevation.epsg) print('temperature grid:', jul.rows, 'x', jul.columns, 'EPSG', jul.epsg) def context(m, *, coast=True): """Add coastlines if Natural Earth is reachable; never raise (keeps the notebook running offline).""" if not coast: return try: m.coastlines(resolution='110m') except Exception as exc: print('coastlines unavailable:', type(exc).__name__)
    elevation grid: 360 x 720 EPSG 4326
temperature grid: 360 x 720 EPSG 4326

    ETOPO relief & bathymetry (NOAA ERDDAP)¶

    ERDDAP serves ETOPO downsampled server-side (a stride on the 1-arc-minute grid) as an ESRI-ASCII grid — a plain-text raster — so we never download the full 466 MB file. We parse the numeric grid with numpy and build the raster with pyramids Dataset.from_array: pyramids is the GIS engine (CRS, reprojection, plotting), numpy just reads numbers from a text file. The result is a global relief field whose negative values are ocean depth.

    In [3]:
    Copied! 
    import numpy as np

# ETOPO180 relief. It arrives from NOAA ERDDAP as a 12 MB ESRI-ASCII grid; the committed copy is
# that grid resampled to 0.5 deg and written as a GeoTIFF, which reads in one call and carries its
# own nodata so the ocean floor does not have to be masked by hand.
relief = Dataset.read_file(str(CACHE / 'etopo_relief.tif'))
vals = np.asarray(relief.read_array(band=0), float)
vals = vals[vals != relief.no_data_value[0]]
print('relief grid:', relief.rows, 'x', relief.columns, 'EPSG', relief.epsg)
print(f'range: {vals.min():.0f} m (deep ocean) .. {vals.max():.0f} m (peaks)')
    import numpy as np # ETOPO180 relief. It arrives from NOAA ERDDAP as a 12 MB ESRI-ASCII grid; the committed copy is # that grid resampled to 0.5 deg and written as a GeoTIFF, which reads in one call and carries its # own nodata so the ocean floor does not have to be masked by hand. relief = Dataset.read_file(str(CACHE / 'etopo_relief.tif')) vals = np.asarray(relief.read_array(band=0), float) vals = vals[vals != relief.no_data_value[0]] print('relief grid:', relief.rows, 'x', relief.columns, 'EPSG', relief.epsg) print(f'range: {vals.min():.0f} m (deep ocean) .. {vals.max():.0f} m (peaks)')

range: -8264 m (deep ocean) .. 5627 m (peaks)

    1. Global elevation on an orthographic globe¶

    ocean() fills the disc, field draws the reprojected DEM (ocean cells are nodata, so the disc shows through the sea), and coastlines() + graticule() finish it. colorbar() adds the elevation scale.

    In [4]:
    Copied! 
    m = Map(crs=projections.orthographic(lon=10, lat=30), globe=True, figsize=(6.5, 6.5))
m.ocean()
m.field(elevation, cmap='terrain', vmin=-1000, vmax=5000)
context(m)
m.graticule(lon_step=30, lat_step=30)
m.set_global()
m.colorbar(label='elevation (m)')
m.set_title('WorldClim elevation - orthographic globe')
m.render()
m.fig;
    m = Map(crs=projections.orthographic(lon=10, lat=30), globe=True, figsize=(6.5, 6.5)) m.ocean() m.field(elevation, cmap='terrain', vmin=-1000, vmax=5000) context(m) m.graticule(lon_step=30, lat_step=30) m.set_global() m.colorbar(label='elevation (m)') m.set_title('WorldClim elevation - orthographic globe') m.render() m.fig;

    2. July temperature — filled contours¶

    contours of the July mean temperature over a globe centred on Asia. The ocean disc shows through where the land grid is nodata.

    In [5]:
    Copied! 
    m = Map(crs=projections.orthographic(lon=80, lat=25), globe=True, figsize=(6.5, 6.5))
m.ocean()
m.contours(jul, cmap='RdYlBu_r', vmin=-40, vmax=40, filled=True)
context(m)
m.graticule(lon_step=30, lat_step=30)
m.set_global()
m.colorbar(label='July mean T (degC)')
m.set_title('WorldClim July temperature - contourf')
m.render()
m.fig;

    3. Whole-world projections¶

    The same data on the two equal-ish world projections. Robinson with pcolormesh, Mollweide with contours — both framed and set to the full domain.

    In [6]:
    Copied! 
    m = Map(crs=projections.robinson(lon=0), globe=True, figsize=(9.5, 5.2))
m.ocean()
m.pcolormesh(jul, cmap='RdYlBu_r', vmin=-40, vmax=40)
context(m)
m.graticule(lon_step=60, lat_step=30)
m.set_global()
m.colorbar(label='July mean T (degC)')
m.set_title('Robinson - pcolormesh')
m.render()
m.fig;

    4. Seasonal contrast — two globes side by side¶

    Map accepts an existing ax, so several globes fit in one figure. January vs July temperature on matching orthographic views shows the hemispheres swapping warmth.

    In [8]:
    Copied! 
    fig, (axL, axR) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 5.6))
for ax, month, label in [(axL, jan, 'January'), (axR, jul, 'July')]:
    m = Map(crs=projections.orthographic(lon=0, lat=0), globe=True, ax=ax)
    m.ocean()
    m.contours(month, cmap='RdYlBu_r', vmin=-40, vmax=40, filled=True)
    context(m)
    m.graticule(lon_step=45, lat_step=30)
    m.set_global()
    m.set_title(f'{label} mean temperature')
    m.render()
fig.tight_layout(); fig;
    fig, (axL, axR) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 5.6)) for ax, month, label in [(axL, jan, 'January'), (axR, jul, 'July')]: m = Map(crs=projections.orthographic(lon=0, lat=0), globe=True, ax=ax) m.ocean() m.contours(month, cmap='RdYlBu_r', vmin=-40, vmax=40, filled=True) context(m) m.graticule(lon_step=45, lat_step=30) m.set_global() m.set_title(f'{label} mean temperature') m.render() fig.tight_layout(); fig;

    5. Centre the globe on a place¶

    The orthographic centre (lon, lat) fixes where the globe faces — change those two numbers to point it anywhere. Below, the same ETOPO relief is shown from four centres. To zoom into a region of a centred globe instead of the whole disc, use set_domain(name) (a named region) or set_bounds(...). set_bounds takes (west, south, east, north) in the display CRS — the same order on every tier, and the one Bounds holds its own numbers in — or, better, a Bounds, which names the CRS as well as the ordering and is reprojected for you: set_bounds(Bounds.from_bbox([xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax], crs=4326)).

    In [9]:
    Copied! 
    places = [('Americas', -90, 15), ('Africa & Europe', 15, 20),
          ('Asia', 95, 30), ('Pacific', -160, 5)]
fig, axs = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(9, 9))
for ax, (name, lon, lat) in zip(axs.ravel(), places):
    m = Map(crs=projections.orthographic(lon=lon, lat=lat), globe=True, ax=ax)
    m.field(relief, cmap='terrain', vmin=-8000, vmax=8000)
    context(m)
    m.graticule(lon_step=30, lat_step=30)
    m.set_global()
    m.set_title(f'{name}  (lon={lon}, lat={lat})')
    m.render()
fig.tight_layout(); fig;
    places = [('Americas', -90, 15), ('Africa & Europe', 15, 20), ('Asia', 95, 30), ('Pacific', -160, 5)] fig, axs = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(9, 9)) for ax, (name, lon, lat) in zip(axs.ravel(), places): m = Map(crs=projections.orthographic(lon=lon, lat=lat), globe=True, ax=ax) m.field(relief, cmap='terrain', vmin=-8000, vmax=8000) context(m) m.graticule(lon_step=30, lat_step=30) m.set_global() m.set_title(f'{name} (lon={lon}, lat={lat})') m.render() fig.tight_layout(); fig;

    Zoom into a region of a centred globe — centre on Europe, then set_domain('europe') to crop the view to Europe's bounds (the data stays clipped to the projection disc):

    In [10]:
    Copied! 
    m = Map(crs=projections.orthographic(lon=10, lat=50), globe=True, figsize=(6.5, 6.5))
m.field(relief, cmap='terrain', vmin=-8000, vmax=8000)
context(m)
m.graticule(lon_step=10, lat_step=10)
m.set_global()
m.colorbar(label='elevation / depth (m)')
m.set_title('centred on Europe, zoomed with set_domain')
m.render()
m.set_domain('europe')   # crop the view to the region's bounds
m.fig;
    m = Map(crs=projections.orthographic(lon=10, lat=50), globe=True, figsize=(6.5, 6.5)) m.field(relief, cmap='terrain', vmin=-8000, vmax=8000) context(m) m.graticule(lon_step=10, lat_step=10) m.set_global() m.colorbar(label='elevation / depth (m)') m.set_title('centred on Europe, zoomed with set_domain') m.render() m.set_domain('europe') # crop the view to the region's bounds m.fig;

    6. ETOPO relief & bathymetry on the globe¶

    Because ETOPO carries ocean depth, the whole globe is data — no ocean() needed. A terrain colormap spanning +/- 8000 m renders the sea floor in blues and the land in greens/browns. Coastlines trace the zero contour.

    In [11]:
    Copied! 
    m = Map(crs=projections.orthographic(lon=-20, lat=20), globe=True, figsize=(6.5, 6.5))
m.field(relief, cmap='terrain', vmin=-8000, vmax=8000)
context(m)
m.graticule(lon_step=30, lat_step=30)
m.set_global()
m.colorbar(label='elevation / depth (m)')
m.set_title('ETOPO relief & bathymetry - orthographic globe')
m.render()
m.fig;
    m = Map(crs=projections.orthographic(lon=-20, lat=20), globe=True, figsize=(6.5, 6.5)) m.field(relief, cmap='terrain', vmin=-8000, vmax=8000) context(m) m.graticule(lon_step=30, lat_step=30) m.set_global() m.colorbar(label='elevation / depth (m)') m.set_title('ETOPO relief & bathymetry - orthographic globe') m.render() m.fig;
    In [12]:
    Copied! 
    m = Map(crs=projections.robinson(lon=0), globe=True, figsize=(9.5, 5.2))
m.field(relief, cmap='terrain', vmin=-8000, vmax=8000)
context(m)
m.graticule(lon_step=60, lat_step=30)
m.set_global()
m.colorbar(label='elevation / depth (m)')
m.set_title('ETOPO relief & bathymetry - Robinson (whole sea floor)')
m.render()
m.fig;
    m = Map(crs=projections.robinson(lon=0), globe=True, figsize=(9.5, 5.2)) m.field(relief, cmap='terrain', vmin=-8000, vmax=8000) context(m) m.graticule(lon_step=60, lat_step=30) m.set_global() m.colorbar(label='elevation / depth (m)') m.set_title('ETOPO relief & bathymetry - Robinson (whole sea floor)') m.render() m.fig;

    7. Save a globe to PNG¶

    save() applies the frame and writes the figure; the data and fills are clipped to the boundary in the file.

    In [13]:
    Copied! 
    out = Path('global_elevation_globe.png')
m = Map(crs=projections.orthographic(lon=-60, lat=10), globe=True, figsize=(6.5, 6.5))
m.ocean()
m.field(elevation, cmap='terrain', vmin=-1000, vmax=5000)
context(m)
m.graticule(); m.set_global()
m.colorbar(label='elevation (m)')
m.save(str(out))
print('saved:', out.resolve(), '|', out.stat().st_size, 'bytes')
out.unlink()  # clean up the example artifact
    out = Path('global_elevation_globe.png') m = Map(crs=projections.orthographic(lon=-60, lat=10), globe=True, figsize=(6.5, 6.5)) m.ocean() m.field(elevation, cmap='terrain', vmin=-1000, vmax=5000) context(m) m.graticule(); m.set_global() m.colorbar(label='elevation (m)') m.save(str(out)) print('saved:', out.resolve(), '|', out.stat().st_size, 'bytes') out.unlink() # clean up the example artifact
